en: be announced in advance; be notified beforehand

examples.ko: 내일 태풍이 올 거라고 미리 예고됐어요.
examples.en: It was announced in advance that a typhoon would hit tomorrow.

examples.ko: 새 드라마의 첫 방송이 예고되고 있어요.
examples.en: The first episode of the new drama is being previewed.

examples.ko: 정전이 예고된 날에는 미리 휴대폰을 충전해 둬요.
examples.en: On days when a power outage is announced, I charge my phone ahead of time.

examples.ko: 회사에 큰 변화가 예고돼서 다들 긴장했어요.
examples.en: A big change at the company was announced, so everyone got nervous.

examples.ko: 눈이 온다고 예고될 때마다 일찍 퇴근해요.
examples.en: Whenever snow is forecast, I leave work early.
The water cut was announced in advance, but I didn't know.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '미리 알려 주다'를 더 자주 써요. '예고되다'는 뉴스, 방송, 공지에서 '정전이 예고되다'처럼 나와요. 알리는 쪽은 '예고하다', 알려지는 일은 '예고되다'예요.
explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say '미리 알려 주다' more often. '예고되다' shows up in news, broadcasts and notices, as in '정전이 예고되다'. The one announcing uses '예고하다'; the thing announced is '예고되다'.

examples.en: That mistake is not easily forgiven.

examples.ko: 거짓말은 어떤 이유로도 용서될 수 없어요.
examples.en: A lie can't be forgiven for any reason.
Because I apologized sincerely, everything was forgiven.
Since he was a child, the mood was that it could be forgiven this time.
I thought breaking the promise had been forgiven.

examples.ko: 사정을 알고 나니 그의 행동이 용서돼요.
examples.en: Now that I know the circumstances, his behavior seems forgivable.

explain: '용서되다'는 '용서가 된다'는 느낌이라 보통 '용서되지 않다', '용서될 수 없다'처럼 부정으로 많이 써요. 내가 누군가를 용서할 때는 '용서하다' 또는 '봐주다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '용서되다' is mostly used in the negative, like '용서되지 않다' or '용서될 수 없다'. When you yourself forgive someone, '용서하다' or the casual '봐주다' sounds more natural.

en: be played back; be regenerated; be recycled; be revived

examples.en: The video plays automatically.
The internet is slow, so the music won't play.
The injured skin regenerated in a few days.
Discarded paper gets recycled into new notebooks.

examples.ko: 재생되는 동안 잠깐 화면을 꺼도 돼요.
examples.en: You can turn off the screen for a moment while it's playing.

examples.ko: 녹음 파일이 잘 재생되는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check whether the recording plays well.

explain: 일상에서는 영상이나 음악이 '재생되다'일 때 가장 많이 써요. 재활용은 '재활용되다'가 더 흔하고, 피부나 조직이 다시 자라는 건 '재생되다'예요. 내가 틀 때는 '재생하다', '틀다'를 써요.
explain_en: Most often it means a video or song 'plays'. For recycling, '재활용되다' is more common; '재생되다' fits skin or tissue growing back. When you start it yourself, say '재생하다' or '틀다'.

examples.en: The salary is paid on the 25th of every month.
The repair fee has already been paid.

examples.ko: 아직 돈이 지불되지 않아서 물건을 못 받았어요.
examples.en: The money hasn't been paid yet, so I couldn't get the item.
If you pay by card, it will be paid automatically.
The amount that has been paid cannot be refunded.
As soon as the deposit is paid, I'll give you the contract.

explain: 말할 때는 '내다'를 가장 많이 써서 '돈을 내다'라고 해요. '지불하다'는 조금 딱딱하고, '지불되다'는 계약서, 영수증, 공지 같은 글에 주로 나와요.
explain_en: In speech people mostly say '돈을 내다'. '지불하다' is a bit formal, and '지불되다' appears mainly in contracts, receipts and notices.

examples.en: What he said sounded false.
A fake smile shows right away.
I later found out that the rumor was untrue.
I apologized with a sincere heart.

examples.ko: 광고 속 이야기가 거짓된 것으로 밝혀졌어요.
examples.en: The story in the ad turned out to be false.

examples.ko: 거짓되고 겉만 번지르르한 말에 속지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't be fooled by fake and showy words.

explain: '거짓말이에요', '가짜예요'를 더 자주 써요. '거짓되다'는 사람의 마음, 말, 웃음이 진실하지 않다는 느낌으로 글이나 조금 무거운 대화에 나와요. 반대말은 '참되다', '진실하다'예요.
explain_en: In daily talk 거짓말이에요 or 가짜예요 are more common. 거짓되다 describes words, smiles, or feelings that are not sincere, mostly in writing or serious talk. Its opposites are 참되다 and 진실하다.

examples.en: The bike had rusted, so I wiped it.

examples.ko: 비를 맞은 못에 녹이 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A lot of rust formed on the nails that got rained on.
If you spray rust remover, it comes off easily.
The old key was covered in rust.

examples.ko: 칼에 녹이 슬지 않게 물기를 닦아 두세요.
examples.en: Wipe off the moisture so the knife doesn't rust.

examples.ko: 다리 난간에 붉은 녹이 올라와 있었어요.
examples.en: Red rust had come up on the bridge railing.

explain: '녹이 슬다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 쇠가 녹는다는 뜻의 '녹다'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 쇠로 된 물건에만 쓰고, 오래 안 써서 둔해진 걸 '녹슬다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: The natural pairing is '녹이 슬다'. It sounds like the verb '녹다' (to melt) but is a different word. It's for metal things, and '녹슬다' is also used for skills that have gone dull from lack of use.

en: be mobilized; be called in; be drawn in

examples.en: All the staff were pulled in to prepare for the festival.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 제설 장비가 동원돼요.
examples.en: Because of heavy snow, snow-clearing equipment is brought out.
I was suddenly roped into cleaning on the weekend.

examples.ko: 큰 행사에는 많은 사람이 동원되는 편이에요.
examples.en: Big events tend to bring in lots of people.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 소방차 열 대가 동원됐어요.
examples.en: Ten fire trucks were sent to the accident scene.

examples.ko: 억지로 동원된 사람들은 표정이 좋지 않았어요.
examples.en: The people who were forced to come didn't look happy.

explain: '동원되다'는 본인이 원해서가 아니라 위에서 시켜서 불려 나간다는 느낌이 있어요. 자기가 스스로 나서면 '참여하다'나 '나서다'를 써요.
explain_en: '동원되다' carries the feeling of being called out by someone above, not volunteering. If you step up on your own, use '참여하다' or '나서다'.

examples.en: I was hired by a big company this year.
I did well in the interview and was hired right away.
New employees are usually hired in March.
The person who was hired starts work next week.
Can I be hired even without experience?
It's rare to be hired just by submitting documents.

explain: '뽑히다'는 말할 때 쓰는 편한 표현이고, '채용되다'는 공식적인 느낌이에요. 회사가 사람을 쓸 때 '채용하다'나 '뽑다'를 쓰고, 합격은 '붙다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '뽑히다' is the casual spoken form; '채용되다' sounds more official. A company says '채용하다' or '뽑다', and passing is also called '붙다'.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 안 쓰는 가구를 처분해요.
examples.en: Before moving, I get rid of the furniture I don't use.

examples.ko: 오래된 차를 처분하고 새 차를 샀어요.
examples.en: I got rid of the old car and bought a new one.
I opened a shop with the money from selling my house.
Trash must be disposed of according to the rules.
We plan to sell off the stock cheaply.
I got rid of the books I didn't need all at once.

explain: '팔다'는 돈을 받고 넘기는 것이고, '버리다'는 그냥 내놓는 것이에요. '처분하다'는 팔거나 버려서 정리한다는 넓은 말이라 집, 차, 재고처럼 큰 물건에 많이 써요.
explain_en: '팔다' means handing over for money and '버리다' means throwing away. '처분하다' covers both as 'getting rid of', and is often used for bigger things such as houses, cars or stock.

examples.en: Smartphones spread quickly.

examples.ko: 전기차가 점점 더 많이 보급되고 있어요.
examples.en: Electric cars are becoming more and more widespread.
As the internet reached the countryside, life got easier.
This app is distributed to schools for free.
The new textbook was handed out to all students.

examples.ko: 보급된 지 얼마 안 된 기술이라 아직 비싸요.
examples.en: The technology isn't widespread yet, so it's still expensive.

explain: '퍼지다'는 소문이나 병에도 쓰지만 '보급되다'는 물건, 기술, 서비스가 널리 쓰이게 될 때 써요. 소문에는 쓰지 않아요. 짝말은 '널리 보급되다'예요.
explain_en: '퍼지다' also fits rumors and diseases, but '보급되다' is for products, technology or services coming into wide use. Don't use it for rumors. A common pairing is '널리 보급되다'.

examples.en: I apply the grammar I learned to real conversations.

examples.ko: 이 레시피를 응용해서 새 요리를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a new dish by adapting this recipe.

examples.ko: 기본 동작을 응용하면 어려운 동작도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you build on the basic moves, you can do hard ones too.
The ability to apply things is built through practice.

examples.ko: 시험에는 배운 내용을 응용해서 푸는 문제가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many questions on the test could be solved by applying what we learned.

examples.ko: 수학 공식을 응용할 줄 알아야 해요.
examples.en: You need to know how to apply math formulas.

explain: '적용하다'는 규칙이나 방법을 그대로 가져다 쓰는 것이고, '응용하다'는 원리를 바탕으로 조금 바꿔서 쓰는 것이에요. '활용하다'는 가진 것을 잘 이용한다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '적용하다' means using a rule or method as is; '응용하다' means adjusting it a bit based on the principle. '활용하다' feels more like making good use of what you have.

examples.ko: 제 첫 번째 책이 다음 달에 출판돼요.
examples.en: My first book will be published next month.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 십 년 전에 출판되었어요.
examples.en: This novel was published ten years ago.

examples.ko: 출판된 책은 서점에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: A published book can be bought at a bookstore.
That poetry collection was also published in English.
It took a year before the manuscript got published.
It became a bestseller as soon as it was published.

explain: '나오다'가 말할 때 더 자연스러워서 '책이 나왔어요'라고 많이 해요. '출판되다'는 책, 잡지 같은 인쇄물에 써요. 인터넷에 올리는 글은 '게시되다', '올라오다'가 맞아요.
explain_en: In speech '책이 나왔어요' sounds more natural. '출판되다' is for printed matter like books and magazines. For things posted online, use '게시되다' or '올라오다'.

examples.en: I obtained my driver's license last year.
Getting a certificate helps with finding a job.
I have a friend who acquired Korean citizenship.
I'm going to graduate school to earn a degree.

examples.ko: 집을 취득할 때는 세금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay tax when you acquire a house.
Please tell me how to earn credits.

explain: 자격증, 면허, 학위, 국적처럼 공식적으로 얻는 것에 써요. 말할 때는 '따다'가 편해서 '자격증을 따다'라고 많이 해요. 물건을 사는 건 '사다'예요.
explain_en: Used for officially gaining a certificate, license, degree or citizenship. In speech, '따다' is easier, as in '자격증을 따다'. For buying things, just use '사다'.

examples.en: In the movie, the villain kidnaps the hero's friend.
I saw news that the criminal kidnapped a child.
Kidnapping a person is a serious crime.
The police caught the man who tried to kidnap someone by car.
In the novel, aliens abduct people.

examples.ko: 납치한 사람을 풀어 주면 처벌이 줄어요.
examples.en: If you release the person you kidnapped, the punishment is reduced.

explain: 뉴스와 영화에서 자주 들리는 말이에요. 비슷한 '유괴하다'는 속여서 아이를 데려가는 것이고, '납치하다'는 힘으로 강제로 데려가는 느낌이에요. 피해 입장은 '납치당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: You hear this a lot in news and films. '유괴하다' is luring away a child by deception, while '납치하다' is taking someone by force. The victim's side is '납치당하다'.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 많이 와서 홍수가 우려돼요.
examples.en: Heavy rain tomorrow raises concerns about flooding.
Voices worried that the economy might get worse grew louder.

examples.ko: 건강 문제가 우려되는 사람은 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If you have health concerns, please see a doctor.
The doctor said side effects are a concern.
Slow down when you are worried about an accident.
I was worried prices would go up, but luckily they stayed the same.

explain: '걱정되다'는 일상에서 누구나 쓰고, '우려되다'는 뉴스, 보고서, 공식적인 말에서 쓰는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. '걱정'은 사람의 마음, '우려'는 앞으로 나쁜 일이 생길 가능성이라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '걱정되다' is the everyday word; '우려되다' is stiffer and appears in news, reports and formal speech. '걱정' is a personal worry, while '우려' is about the possibility of something bad happening.

examples.ko: 회사는 새 직원을 빨리 정착시키려고 노력해요.
examples.en: The company tries hard to help new employees settle in quickly.

examples.ko: 좋은 습관을 정착시키는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time to establish a good habit.
They settled the refugee family in this village.

examples.ko: 새 제도를 정착시킨 사람은 바로 팀장님이에요.
examples.en: The person who got the new system established is the team leader.
To make it a lasting culture, you have to keep doing it for a long time.
I wanted to settle the kids in one place.

explain: '정착하다'는 스스로 자리를 잡는 것이고, '정착시키다'는 다른 사람이나 제도, 습관을 자리 잡게 하는 것이에요. '정착되다'는 저절로 자리 잡은 결과를 말해요.
explain_en: '정착하다' is settling by oneself; '정착시키다' is making a person, system or habit take root. '정착되다' describes the result of something having taken root.

examples.en: The hospital billed me for the treatment.
I'm going to claim the repair cost from the insurance company.
I got back the money the shop charged by mistake.

examples.ko: 서류를 내면 환불을 청구할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you submit the documents, you can claim a refund.
I was surprised when the landlord billed me for repairs.
We will bill you for the cost next month.

explain: 말할 때는 '달라고 하다'로 풀어 쓰기도 해요. 돈을 공식적으로 요구하는 자리, 예를 들어 요금·보험금·비용에서 써요. 요금 안내서는 '청구서', 돈을 내는 쪽은 '내다'나 '지불하다'를 써요.
explain_en: In speech people often say '달라고 하다' instead. It is used in official demands for money, such as fees, insurance payouts and costs. The bill is a '청구서', and the paying side uses '내다' or '지불하다'.

examples.en: The misty lake looked mysterious.
That actor has a mysterious air about him.
The aurora in the night sky is truly mysterious.
I was drawn into the mysterious and beautiful music.

examples.ko: 작은 씨앗이 자라는 모습이 신비스럽게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Watching a tiny seed grow feels wondrous.
The inside of the cave was mysterious, but a little scary.

explain: '신비롭다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. '이상하다', '수상하다'는 나쁜 느낌이 있지만 '신비스럽다'는 알 수 없어서 궁금하고 아름답다는 좋은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '신비롭다'. Unlike '이상하다' or '수상하다', which feel negative, '신비스럽다' feels positive: unknowable, intriguing and beautiful.

examples.en: This bus runs from 5 a.m.

examples.ko: 눈이 와서 지하철이 천천히 운행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of the snow, the subway is running slowly.
Some routes don't run on public holidays.
Is there a bus that runs at night too?

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 기차가 모두 운행되지 않았어요.
examples.en: No trains ran because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 이 열차는 하루에 열 번 운행될 거예요.
examples.en: This train will run ten times a day.

explain: 버스, 지하철, 기차, 배처럼 정해진 길을 다니는 탈것에 써요. 개인 차를 몰면 '운전하다'라고 하고, '운행'은 운영하는 쪽 입장이에요. 짝말은 '운행이 중단되다'예요.
explain_en: For buses, subways, trains and ships that follow set routes. Driving your own car is '운전하다'; '운행' is from the operator's side. A common pairing is '운행이 중단되다'.

examples.en: I printed out the meeting materials and handed them out.
I have to bring a printed-out plane ticket.
The printer broke, so I couldn't print.

examples.ko: 파일을 열어서 출력하는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please show me how to open the file and print it.

examples.ko: 흑백으로 출력하면 잉크를 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you print in black and white, you can save ink.
This program displays the result on the screen.

explain: 말할 때는 '프린트하다', '뽑다'가 아주 흔해서 '서류 좀 뽑아 주세요'라고 해요. '출력하다'는 조금 딱딱하고, 컴퓨터가 결과를 화면에 내보낼 때도 써요. 반대로 넣는 건 '입력하다'예요.
explain_en: In speech '프린트하다' and '뽑다' are very common, as in '서류 좀 뽑아 주세요'. '출력하다' is a bit stiffer and also covers a computer displaying results. The opposite is '입력하다'.

examples.en: The representatives of the two countries will hold talks tomorrow.
The president held talks with the head of an overseas company.
The reporters waited outside while the talks went on.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 가격 문제로 다시 회담하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two companies decided to talk again about the price.
The result of the talks will be announced in the afternoon.
We had no time to meet and hold talks.

explain: 나라나 큰 단체의 대표가 공식적으로 만나 이야기할 때 써요. 친구나 동료와 하는 이야기에는 '이야기하다', 회사 일에는 '미팅하다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 '회담을 하다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when representatives of countries or large organizations meet officially. For friends or colleagues, '이야기하다' is natural, and '미팅하다' for business. People usually say '회담을 하다'.

examples.en: The man was indicted on fraud charges.
A person who is indicted goes to trial.
He wasn't charged because there wasn't enough evidence.
The news said the company's head was indicted.
The lawyer said an indictment is likely.

examples.ko: 세 명이 한꺼번에 기소되는 일이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a case where three people were indicted at once.

explain: 주로 뉴스에서 들리는 법률 말이에요. 검사가 재판에 넘기는 것을 '기소하다', 넘겨지는 사람은 '기소되다'라고 해요. '체포되다'는 경찰이 잡는 것이라 달라요.
explain_en: A legal term mostly heard in the news. The prosecutor 'files charges' with '기소하다'; the person charged is '기소되다'. '체포되다' is different: it is being arrested by police.

examples.ko: 검사가 그 사람을 사기 혐의로 기소했어요.
examples.en: The prosecutor indicted him on fraud charges.
I heard they decided to prosecute because the evidence was enough.
The prosecution plans to indict three people.
The case in which the company was prosecuted was on the news.

examples.ko: 피해자가 원하지 않아도 기소하는 경우가 있어요.
examples.en: There are cases where they prosecute even if the victim doesn't want it.
The prosecutor gathers evidence in order to indict.

explain: 주어는 거의 항상 '검사'나 '검찰'이에요. 일반 사람이 고소하는 건 '고소하다'이고, 검사가 재판에 넘기는 건 '기소하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스에서 들려요.
explain_en: The subject is almost always a prosecutor. A private person filing a complaint is '고소하다', while a prosecutor taking the case to court is '기소하다'. Rare in daily talk, common in news.

examples.en: I was persuaded by my friend's sincere words.
I'm the kind of person who gets persuaded easily.

examples.ko: 설명을 듣고 나니 설득될 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: After hearing the explanation, I couldn't help but be convinced.
No matter what I said, he wasn't persuaded.
My parents, once persuaded, finally gave permission.
If you show the data, the other person gets convinced.

explain: '설득하다'는 설득하는 사람, '설득되다'는 마음이 바뀐 사람의 입장이에요. 말할 때는 '넘어가다', '마음이 바뀌다'도 많이 써요. '이해되다'는 뜻을 알겠다는 것이라 달라요.
explain_en: '설득하다' is the persuader's side; '설득되다' is the side whose mind was changed. In speech, '넘어가다' or '마음이 바뀌다' are also common. '이해되다' is different: it only means 'it makes sense'.

en: play an active role; perform brilliantly

examples.ko: 그 선수는 이번 경기에서 크게 활약했어요.
examples.en: That player had a great game this time.
My younger brother is a star as the school's representative.
There are many Korean singers active overseas.
The new employee shone in the project and was praised.
I look forward to seeing you do great things in the future.
The actors who shone in the film received awards.

explain: 결과가 눈에 띄게 좋을 때 써서, 칭찬하는 말이에요. 스포츠 선수, 연예인, 직장에서 큰 몫을 한 사람에게 '활약했다'고 하면 좋은 평가예요. '크게 활약하다', '맹활약하다'처럼 정도를 붙여서도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when someone's results clearly stand out, so it is praise. Saying '활약했다' about an athlete, an entertainer or a colleague who played a big part is a good review. People often add degree words, as in '크게 활약하다' and '맹활약하다'.

examples.ko: 이 사건에 누군가 개입된 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems somebody was involved in this incident.

examples.ko: 제 감정이 개입되면 공정하게 판단하기 어려워요.
examples.en: If my feelings get involved, it's hard to judge fairly.
There's no evidence that the company was involved.
Be careful not to let personal reasons creep in.
Many people got involved, and things became complicated.
The more human hands get involved, the more the result changes.

explain: '끼어들다'는 대화나 줄에 끼는 일상적인 말이고, '개입되다'는 어떤 일에 다른 사람이나 요소가 들어와 영향을 주는 것이에요. 좋은 일보다는 문제가 되는 일에 많이 써요.
explain_en: '끼어들다' is the everyday word for cutting into a conversation or a line. '개입되다' is when a person or factor enters a matter and affects it, more often in problematic situations than good ones.

examples.ko: 새 기능의 구현은 다음 달에 끝나요.
examples.en: The implementation of the new feature will finish next month.
It takes time to carry an idea through to implementation.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 간단한 구현으로도 잘 작동해요.
examples.en: This app works well even with a simple implementation.
My goal is the realization of my dream.

examples.ko: 구현이 어려운 부분은 나중에 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to do the hard-to-implement part later.
One person handled both the design and implementation.

explain: 개발자들이 '기능 구현'이라고 많이 써요. 계획을 실제로 만들어 내는 것이고, 말로는 '만들다', '실현하다'도 써요. '구현'은 명사라 '구현하다', '구현되다'로 바꿔 써요.
explain_en: Developers say '기능 구현' constantly. It means turning a plan into something real; in speech '만들다' or '실현하다' also work. It's a noun, with '구현하다' and '구현되다' as verb forms.

en: be realized; be implemented; be embodied

examples.en: The new feature will be implemented next week.
The designer's idea was realized just as it was.

examples.ko: 꿈이 현실로 구현되는 날이 올 거예요.
examples.en: The day will come when the dream becomes reality.
This feature hasn't been implemented yet.
The world in the game was recreated as if it were real.
Please wait until the plan is carried out.

explain: '만들어지다'보다 딱딱하고, 계획이나 아이디어, 기능이 실제로 나타난다는 말이에요. 컴퓨터, 디자인, 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요. 만드는 쪽은 '구현하다'예요.
explain_en: Stiffer than '만들어지다'; it says a plan, idea or feature has actually appeared. Common in talk about computing, design and policy. The maker's side is '구현하다'.

examples.en: The bird is pecking the tree with its beak.
An eagle's beak is very sharp.

examples.ko: 아기 새가 노란 부리를 크게 벌렸어요.
examples.en: The baby bird opened its yellow beak wide.
Ducks have flat bills.
Parrots have curved beaks.
The magpie flew off with a twig in its beak.

explain: 새의 입 부분이에요. 사람에게는 '입', 동물에게는 '주둥이'를 쓰는데, 새만은 '부리'라고 해요. 사람 입을 낮춰서 '주둥이'라고 하면 실례가 돼요.
explain_en: A bird's mouth part. Humans have '입' and many animals '주둥이', but birds alone have '부리'. Calling a person's mouth '주둥이' is rude.

en: be appointed; be selected for a post

examples.en: Department head Kim was appointed as the new team leader.
Let me introduce the person who was appointed society president.
He was unanimously chosen as the representative.

examples.ko: 새 감독이 선임되면 팀이 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: When a new coach is appointed, the team will change.
An outside expert is appointed as a committee member.
As soon as he was appointed, he started reforms.

explain: 회사나 단체에서 사람이 어떤 자리를 맡도록 정해질 때 써요. 말로는 '뽑히다', '임명되다'도 써요. '선임'은 순서가 먼저인 사람, 즉 선배라는 뜻도 있으니 문장을 잘 봐야 해요.
explain_en: Used when a person is chosen for a post in a company or organization. In speech '뽑히다' or '임명되다' also work. Note that '선임' can also mean a senior person, so read the context.

examples.en: I stocked up on a lot of ramen during the sale.

examples.ko: 태풍이 온다고 해서 물을 쟁여 놨어요.
examples.en: A typhoon was coming, so I stored up water.
I have a habit of stocking the fridge with side dishes.
Grandmother keeps rice stored up in the shed.

examples.ko: 책을 방에 쟁이면 걸어 다니기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you pile books up in the room, it's hard to walk around.

examples.ko: 좋아하는 과자를 쟁일 수 있어서 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm happy I can stock up on my favorite snacks.

explain: '쌓다'는 위로 높이 올리는 것이고, '쟁이다'는 나중에 쓰려고 많이 모아 두는 것이에요. 말할 때는 '쟁여 두다', '쟁여 놓다'로 많이 쓰고, 할인할 때 사 두는 것을 '쟁이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '쌓다' is stacking things up high; '쟁이다' is stockpiling a lot for later use. In speech it's usually '쟁여 두다' or '쟁여 놓다', and also for buying extra on sale.

examples.en: Colds spread easily through coughing.
The good news spread fast.

examples.ko: 한국 문화는 전 세계로 전파되고 있어요.
examples.en: Korean culture is spreading around the world.
Wash your hands so the virus doesn't spread.
I was surprised by how fast the rumor spread.
Buddhism was transmitted to Korea via China.

explain: '퍼지다'가 일상에서 가장 자연스러워요. '전파되다'는 병, 소식, 문화가 한 곳에서 다른 곳으로 옮겨 가는 느낌으로 뉴스와 글에서 써요. 소리가 같은 '전파'는 전자기 신호를 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: '퍼지다' is the most natural in daily talk. '전파되다' suits illness, news and culture moving from one place to another, in news and writing. '전파' as a noun also means radio waves, a separate meaning.

examples.en: I'm so excited about going on a trip tomorrow.
I got more excited as the final approached.
He delivered the news in an excited voice.

examples.ko: 너무 흥분되어서 밤에 잠이 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I was so excited that I couldn't sleep at night.
I took a deep breath to calm my excited heart.

examples.ko: 흥분될 때는 천천히 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When you're worked up, it's good to speak slowly.

explain: '신나다', '설레다'는 기분 좋은 설렘이고, '흥분되다'는 기쁨뿐 아니라 화가 났을 때도 몸과 마음이 달아오르는 느낌이에요. 그래서 문맥을 보고 좋은 흥분인지 나쁜 흥분인지 알아야 해요.
explain_en: '신나다' and '설레다' are happy excitement; '흥분되다' is being worked up in body and mind, which can come from joy or from anger. Context tells you which.

examples.en: The news got the fans very excited.
It was a performance that thrilled the audience.

examples.ko: 아이를 너무 흥분시키면 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: If you get a child too wound up, he can't sleep.
Don't wind up an angry person even more.
He spoke loudly and stirred people up.

examples.ko: 개를 흥분시킬 수 있으니 조용히 하세요.
examples.en: Be quiet, because you might get the dog worked up.

explain: 기분 좋은 쪽은 '신나게 하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '흥분시키다'는 사람이나 동물을 가라앉히기 어렵게 들뜨게 하거나 화나게 할 때 주로 써요. '너무 흥분시키지 마세요'처럼 조심하라는 말과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: For a pleasant mood '신나게 하다' sounds more natural. '흥분시키다' is mostly used when someone is made so worked up or angry that they are hard to calm down, whether a person or an animal. It often comes with a warning, as in '너무 흥분시키지 마세요'.

examples.en: The guard watches the building all night.
Many people were guarding the entrance of the concert hall.
When I was a college student, I guarded a warehouse.
The police are securing the event site.
I signed up for a service that watches over my house.
There aren't enough people to guard, so the work is hard.

explain: 건물, 행사장 같은 곳을 지키는 일이에요. '지키다'는 더 넓게 쓰고, '경비'는 직업 이름이에요. 아파트에서는 '경비원' 또는 '경비 아저씨'라고 불러요. '경비'에는 비용이라는 다른 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: It means guarding buildings or event venues. '지키다' is broader, and '경비' is also a job name; apartment guards are called '경비원' or '경비 아저씨'. Note that '경비' also means expenses, a different word.

examples.en: The factory emits smoke.
You must put out trash on the designated days.
The body releases heat through sweat.

examples.ko: 이 대학은 훌륭한 인재를 많이 배출했어요.
examples.en: This university has produced many fine talents.

examples.ko: 차가 배출하는 가스를 줄이는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to reduce the gas that cars emit.
Please put out food waste separately.

explain: 안에 있는 것을 밖으로 내보내는 말이에요. 쓰레기는 '버리다'가 일상적이고, 분리수거에서는 '배출하다'가 공식 표현이에요. 공장의 연기와 가스, 몸의 땀과 노폐물에도 써요. 학교나 팀에서 인재나 선수가 계속 나오는 것도 '배출하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means sending something inside out. For trash, '버리다' is everyday while '배출하다' is the official term in recycling rules. It also fits factory smoke and gas, and sweat and waste leaving the body. It is also used for a school or team 'producing' talented people one after another.

examples.en: A construction company is selling new apartments.
The owner gave away the puppies for free.
I went to the model house to see the apartments for sale.

examples.ko: 고양이를 분양하려고 키울 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I want to give my cat away, so I'm looking for someone to take it in.

examples.ko: 올해 분양한 집은 벌써 다 팔렸어요.
examples.en: The homes put on sale this year have already sold out.
They aren't puppies raised for giving away.

explain: 새 아파트를 처음 파는 건 '분양하다'이고, 이미 산 집을 다시 파는 건 '팔다'예요. 반려동물을 다른 집에 보내 줄 때도 '분양하다'라고 하는데, 이때는 돈을 받을 수도 있고 무료일 수도 있어요.
explain_en: A developer selling new apartments for the first time is '분양하다'; reselling a home you own is '팔다'. It's also used for finding homes for pets, either free or for a fee.

examples.en: This fruit is distributed across the country.
Fake goods are circulating in the market.
These vegetables go straight from the farm, so they're fresh.

examples.ko: 유통된 지 오래된 제품은 사지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't buy products that have been on the market for a long time.
False information circulated on the internet.

examples.ko: 새 음료는 다음 달부터 편의점에서 유통될 거예요.
examples.en: The new drink will be on sale at convenience stores from next month.

explain: 물건이 만든 곳에서 가게를 거쳐 소비자에게 가는 흐름이에요. 말로는 '팔리다', '나오다'를 쓰기도 해요. 식품 포장에 '유통 기한'이 적혀 있는데, 가게에서 팔 수 있는 마지막 날이에요.
explain_en: Goods flow from the producer through shops to consumers. In speech, '팔리다' or '나오다' are used too. Food packages show '유통 기한', the last date a shop may sell it.

examples.en: My idea was adopted at the meeting.
The adopted plan takes effect from next week.

examples.ko: 이 의견이 최종안으로 채택될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This opinion looks likely to be adopted as the final plan.
I was glad that my writing was picked for the newspaper.
Proposals that weren't adopted are also valuable opinions.
It's a message board where good answers are selected.

explain: 여러 가지 안 중에서 하나가 골라져 쓰이게 될 때 써요. '선택되다'보다 공식적이고, 의견, 방안, 제안에 많이 써요. 사람을 뽑는 경우는 '채용되다'와 구별하세요.
explain_en: Used when one among several options is picked for use. More official than '선택되다', and common for opinions, plans and proposals. Don't confuse it with '채용되다', which is for hiring people.

examples.en: The company adopted my opinion.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 새 교과서를 채택하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our school decided to adopt a new textbook.
The president took the cheapest method.
If we adopt this method, costs go down.
Please tell me what the criteria for adopting are.
The answer the teacher chose was the correct one.

explain: 여러 안 중에서 하나를 골라 쓴다는 말이에요. '선택하다'가 개인 취향이나 일상에 어울리고, '채택하다'는 회의, 학교, 회사에서 방안을 정할 때 어울려요. 쓰는 사람은 힘 있는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: It means picking one option to use. '선택하다' fits personal preferences and daily life; '채택하다' fits meetings, schools and companies deciding on plans. The subject is usually the party with authority.

examples.en: I chatted with my friend all night.

examples.ko: 저는 해외에 사는 가족과 자주 채팅해요.
examples.en: I often chat with my family living abroad.
You shouldn't chat during class.
I missed the bus while chatting.

examples.ko: 새로 알게 된 친구와 채팅하는 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm chatting with a friend I just met.

examples.ko: 오늘은 시간이 없어서 길게 채팅할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I don't have time today, so I can't chat for long.

explain: 요즘은 '채팅하다'보다 '톡하다', '카톡하다', '메시지 보내다'를 더 자주 말해요. '채팅'은 인터넷에서 글자로 실시간으로 이야기하는 것이고, 목소리로 하면 '통화하다'예요.
explain_en: These days '톡하다', '카톡하다' or '메시지 보내다' are more common than '채팅하다'. Chatting means typing back and forth in real time online; by voice it is '통화하다'.

examples.en: The exam is over, so I'm free from studying.
When I leave work, I feel freed from it.
I'm free from a long worry, so I feel at ease.
Korea was liberated from Japan in 1945.

examples.ko: 집안일에서 해방될 수 있는 방법이 없을까요?
examples.en: Isn't there a way to get free from housework?
The liberated people came out to the streets and rejoiced.

explain: 일상에서는 '벗어나다', '자유로워지다'를 쓰고, '해방되다'는 힘들던 일이나 억압에서 벗어난 기쁨을 크게 말할 때 써요. 역사 이야기에서는 1945년 광복을 '해방'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: In daily life '벗어나다' or '자유로워지다' fit; '해방되다' stresses the joy of escaping something hard or oppressive. In history, the 1945 liberation is also called '해방'.

examples.en: Difficulties get overcome as time passes.
My fear is being overcome little by little.

examples.ko: 가난은 노력만으로 극복되지 않을 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes poverty isn't overcome by effort alone.
I judged that the problem had been overcome.
I believe it's a problem that can be overcome.
The crisis was overcome with everyone's help.

explain: '이겨 내다'는 말로 많이 쓰고, '극복하다'는 내가 노력해서 이기는 것이에요. '극복되다'는 노력한 사람보다 문제가 해결된 결과에 초점을 둬서 글이나 뉴스에서 나와요.
explain_en: In speech '이겨 내다' is common; '극복하다' is overcoming something through your own effort. '극복되다' focuses on the problem having been resolved rather than who did it, and shows up in writing and news.
